mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each shareholder, associate, manager, and ultimate beneficial owner for UBO identification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Consular office, notary public, or national civil registry of the investor's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and current register of directors/shareholders for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent corporate authority of the parent jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the French attorney-in-fact, domiciliation provider, and notary for incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds evidence for the share capital contribution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Independent statutory auditor or valuation expert registered in France
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No authentication required if French expert; otherwise Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders and UBOs against the French FIU (TRACFIN) AML/CFT registers, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, and the French national list of politically exposed persons under Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Article L.561-5 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for any PEP, residential address mismatch, use of trust or offshore vehicle, or inconsistent source-of-funds declarations. The French registered agent, domiciliation company, and banks apply these protocols as a precondition to incorporation and account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe - Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the INPI Guichet unique services (www.infogreffe.fr / www.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All incorporation documents, including the corporate name (dénomination sociale), must be submitted in French. The name must be expressed in Latin characters and in a French-readable form; any foreign-script name must be transliterated or accompanied by a French translation. Product brand names may remain in English, but the registered SARL legal name must appear in French or in a globally accepted Latin transliteration on all statutory filings.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: État, République, municipalité, commune, collectivité territoriale (requires prior ministerial or prefectural authorization)
Banque, établissement de crédit, finance, assurance, mutuelle (requires ACPR licence or formal authorization)
Avocat, notaire, membre d'une profession juridique réglementée (requires bar or professional order authorization)
Croix-Rouge, ONU, NATO, organisation internationale (requires international body or state authorization)
Loterie, casino, jeux d'argent (requires National Gaming Authority licence)
France, français, national (may require demonstration of de facto French establishment and non-misleading character)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a corrected or revised name through the Guichet unique without penalty. An administrative appeal must be filed by formal letter or through the portal with the competent registry director (greffe) within 15 days of receipt of the refusal, citing the specific legal grounds of error or violation of Article L.123-2 of the Commercial Code. If administrative refusal is maintained, judicial recourse may be brought before the competent Tribunal de commerce (commercial court) or, for public-order objections, the administrative tribunal, within two months of the final rejection notice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with statutory restrictions. The SARL must have its registered office (siège social) in France. A professional domiciliation company may provide the registered office address, provided the company has a physical French establishment, mail receipt capacity, and statutory documents accessible on site. For a remote AI-pet-robot assembly and trading company, virtual office domiciliation through an authorized domiciliation provider is accepted; a mere PO Box is not sufficient. All corporate records, UBO declarations, and accounting records must be physically maintainable at the French registered address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low statutory inspection probability of approximately 5% annually for a low-risk ISIC 3240 business. ISIC 3240 (toys/games manufacture) may attract consumer-safety inspections by DGCCRF, with an estimated additional 5-8% probability if products are imported or placed on the EU market with CE marking requirements. There is no routine ex-ante inspection for a private SARL, but unannounced inspections occur upon tax audit, customs sampling, or consumer complaint.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed due-diligence compliance fee under prevailing market rates

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL provisions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and Formulaire M (Registration Form)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; capital must be fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in kind. Cash contributions must be paid up at least 20% at incorporation, remainder within 5 years. No escrow account required if capital is fully paid at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders of the SARL hereby approve the subscription of the share capital as set forth in the Articles of Association; that the registered office be established at [address]; and that [Name] be appointed as Manager (Gérant) with full powers to act on behalf of the company in all matters, subject to the statutory and regulatory provisions. The Manager is hereby authorized to complete all formalities for incorporation, including filing with the RCS, publishing legal notices, and opening bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional unless real estate contribution) or private deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts (Articles of Association) in French, including company name, registered office address, share capital, share distribution, management structure, and purpose. If real estate is contributed, notarization is mandatory. Otherwise, a private deed signed by all shareholders is sufficient.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the statuts due to missing information, correct and resubmit within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Share Capital and Obtain Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the company's name and deposit the cash portion of the share capital. Obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) from the bank, which is required for registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays, request a written confirmation and escalate to the bank's compliance department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Legal Notice in a Legal Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales - JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice of incorporation in a legal gazette authorized in the department of the registered office. The notice must include the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, business purpose, and manager details.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette rejects the notice, correct the content and republish.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) or directly with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Formulaire M, statuts, bank certificate, legal notice publication proof, and manager's declaration of no criminal record. The CFE forwards the dossier to the RCS. The RCS issues a K-bis extract upon approval.
required_dossiers: Manager's declaration of no criminal record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, respond within 15 days with additional documents or corrections. If rejected, rectify and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain K-bis Extract and Complete Post-Registration Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, the RCS issues the K-bis extract, which serves as the official proof of incorporation. The company must then register for social security (URSSAF), obtain a SIRET number, and open a permanent bank account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis is delayed, contact the registry and request expedited issuance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no specific industrial license required for toy assembly under French law

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique (via DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - activity below ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) thresholds for light assembly

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), French Public Finances Directorate; official portal: impots.gouv.fr. VAT and corporate tax registration for businesses is administered through the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); customs export and import controls are administered by Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a standard SARL, statutory registration is completed at incorporation through formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, automatically generating SIREN/SIRET legal identifiers and an active corporate tax account with DGFiP. The DGFiP allocates the intra-Community VAT number when the entity begins or plans taxable French supplies. A non-established foreign entity must file a French VAT registration dossier with the competent SIE containing certified incorporation documents, proof of foreign tax residence, bank details, description of intended French operations, and a fiscal representative’s power of attorney if required. Upon approval, the entity receives a numéro de TVA intracommunautaire and must separately obtain an EORI number from DGDDI for customs export declaration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A French SARL is a capital company subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) on its worldwide profits from actual French operations; profits of foreign permanent establishments may be excluded under France’s territoriality rule. For VAT, the SARL is a separate taxable person in its own right. A non-resident owner does not alter the entity’s default legal-form-based classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not apply US-style check-the-box elections; legal form determines tax treatment. Statutory elections available include: (i) a qualifying small SARL may opt for pass-through taxation under personal income tax for a limited period under Article 239 bis AA of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI); (ii) a 95% parent company may elect group tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI; (iii) financially integrated entities may elect VAT group treatment as a single taxable person under Article 1693 ter CGI; (iv) hybrid mismatch rules under the ATAD implementation prevent mismatched deduction outcomes but do not provide elective entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 annual taxable turnover for French-established suppliers of goods and EUR 37,500 for service suppliers under the franchise en base de TVA (small-business VAT exemption); non-established foreign suppliers have no de minimis threshold and must register for French VAT before making taxable supplies in France unless the transaction is reverse-charged to a French VAT-registered customer or falls under the OSS/IOSS special schemes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured electronic invoicing for domestic B2B transactions is phased in by law: large taxpayers from 1 September 2026 and small/medium taxpayers from 1 September 2027 via accredited Tax Dematerialisation Providers (PDPs) connected to the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF). Invoices must be transmitted in CII, UBL or FACTUR-X formats. There is no real-time pre-clearance stamp; e-reporting is transmitted periodically to DGFiP, while exchange data and transaction-status metadata must be preserved for audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: 0% French VAT applies to supplies physically exported outside France and the EU, provided the seller has the power to dispose of the goods, transport is arranged by the seller or on behalf of the foreign customer, and the goods leave EU customs territory under a completed DGDDI export declaration (EX). Services sufficiently linked to exported goods (e.g., loading, transport, ancillary handling) or performed on foreign immovable property may also be zero-rated; B2B cross-border services to a non-EU recipient generally have place of supply in the customer’s country and are invoiced outside French VAT. Intra-EU B2B dispatches are VAT-exempt in France subject to customer VAT-ID validation and EC Sales List reporting. Refund of residual input VAT or recovery through French VAT returns requires matching export invoices to customs evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (EX / déclaration en douane) accepted by DGDDI
Transport evidence: bill of lading, CMR, airway bill or equivalent international consignment note
Inward remittance certificate / bank SWIFT confirmation of payment received from the foreign buyer
Commercial invoice and sales contract with clearly identified foreign customer
Packing list and, where applicable, insurance certificate evidencing physical movement outside the EU
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French tax administration may re-invoice VAT on export if documentation does not substantiate physical exit within the required period or if payments are not repatriated by the 180-day deadline. On audit, DGFiP verifies EX data against manifests and bank statements; denial of zero-rating generates a VAT assessment plus late-payment interest and administrative penalties (40% for insufficient declarations; 80% for deliberate dissimulation or bad faith under Articles 1728–1729 CGI). Fraudulent export-credit claims or sham export schemes also carry criminal exposure under Article 1741 CGI and customs-fraud provisions, including heavy fines and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the monetary authority of the European Central Bank. France has no separate foreign-exchange administration imposing general exchange controls on ordinary corporate transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax-reporting, and prudential controls. A French SARL may receive foreign investment, hold foreign-currency accounts, pay non-resident suppliers, receive export proceeds, distribute dividends, repay shareholder loans, and remit profits without prior foreign-exchange approval. Dividend and interest remittances remain subject to corporate-law requirements, distributable-profit and reserve rules, withholding-tax analysis, beneficial-owner verification, treaty eligibility, bank compliance review, and documentation evidencing the underlying transaction. Banks may delay or reject transactions involving sanctioned parties, high-risk jurisdictions, opaque ownership, inconsistent commercial rationale, or inadequate source-of-funds evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no statutory mandatory surrender requirement, no general requirement to convert export proceeds into euros, and no prescribed conversion ratio or universal statutory deadline for repatriating export receipts. Export proceeds may remain in euros or foreign currency and may be credited to accounts in France or abroad, subject to accounting, tax, customs, sanctions, AML, and bank-reporting obligations. The company should retain contracts, invoices, customs declarations, transport evidence, payment confirmations, and reconciliation records. Large or unusual cross-border payments may be subject to bank information requests and applicable statistical, tax, or regulatory reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection, card acquiring, SEPA transfers, and limited multi-currency balances; Low to Medium as a substitute for a principal French relationship bank. An EU-authorised electronic-money institution or payment institution may passport services into France, but it is not a bank and generally cannot accept deposits or provide unrestricted credit. Account safeguarding, payment-services terms, transaction limits, settlement timing, chargeback exposure, sanctions screening, and fund-freezing rights must be reviewed. Offshore digital EMIs outside the EEA may require an EU-authorised intermediary, local licensing, or a regulated correspondent arrangement and should not be used to evade French or EU AML, sanctions, tax, or payment-reporting requirements. Stripe and similar providers should be treated as payment-service and acquiring channels, not as the company's sole treasury bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal in-person director-attendance requirement for ordinary corporate bank-account opening. Remote onboarding may be available, particularly for straightforward EU-resident ownership structures, using qualified or bank-approved electronic identification. Each bank may require an in-person meeting, video interview, notarised or certified documents, French translations, local contact details, or additional verification. The legal representative, all beneficial owners, authorised signatories, and relevant controlling persons must be identified. A capital-deposit account for incorporation is commonly opened before registration and converted after delivery of the final registration extract and constitutional documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or incomplete beneficial-ownership chain, including a foreign parent, nominee shareholder, trust, foundation, or layered holding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles and shareholder register; group organisation chart to natural-person beneficial owners; certificates of incorporation and good standing for each corporate shareholder; passports and address evidence for beneficial owners and directors; signed beneficial-owner declaration; explanation of control rights and ownership percentages; relevant trust or nominee documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership, non-resident director, or no established French operating footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French registration extract or incorporation filing; registered-office agreement; management and service agreements; business plan; lease, warehouse, or fulfilment evidence where applicable; employment or contractor plan; customer and supplier pipeline; explanation of French commercial activity and expected transaction geography.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Interactive AI robotic-animal business classified as technology, electronics, toy, dual-use, or higher-risk export activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product description; technical specification and bill of materials; end-use statement; product-safety and CE compliance roadmap; customs classification analysis; supplier and manufacturer list; sanctions and export-control screening policy; statement confirming absence of military, surveillance, biometric, or prohibited end use where accurate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected card, Stripe, marketplace, or e-commerce volume inconsistent with stated revenue model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Revenue model; sales forecasts by country and channel; website and terms of sale; acquiring agreements; expected average ticket and refund rate; chargeback controls; customer-verification and fraud-monitoring procedures; VAT and distance-selling analysis; reconciliation process between payment processors and bank accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound shareholder funding, intercompany loans, or payments from unrelated third parties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital-increase or shareholder-loan agreement; board or shareholder resolutions; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; audited or management accounts; originating-bank evidence; tax treatment memorandum; payment-purpose narrative; beneficial-owner confirmation for the remitter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned countries, sanctioned persons, or unusual intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty identification; sanctions-screening results; end-use and end-user certificates; purchase orders and invoices; transport and customs documentation; ownership attestations; documented escalation and approval record; evidence that no sanctioned party benefits from the transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient explanation of expected foreign-currency flows, cash exposure, or circular transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month cash-flow forecast by currency; expected inbound and outbound corridors; treasury policy; intercompany-pricing policy; bank-account map; payment approval matrix; reconciliation controls; explanation of any foreign-currency accounts and hedging strategy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency among registration data, tax records, business activity, beneficial-owner information, or bank application forms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Latest Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence; articles and amendments; tax registration evidence; accounting records; management representation letter; corrected corporate-information pack; written explanation of historical discrepancies and remediation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity through a regulated bank to the SARL's designated capital-deposit account before incorporation or capital increase, using the exact legal entity name and a clear payment reference such as 'capital contribution' or 'capital increase'. For a post-incorporation contribution, transfer funds to the operational account only after the required corporate resolutions and filings. Route shareholder or intercompany debt under a signed loan agreement with principal, maturity, interest, repayment, transfer-pricing, and withholding-tax terms. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments and SWIFT cross-border transfers for non-SEPA currencies. Provide the bank with the subscription or loan agreement, corporate resolutions, source-of-funds evidence, ownership chart, and expected-use schedule. There is no general French statutory capital purpose-code regime; banks may require internal purpose codes or ISO 20022 purpose information. Reconcile the bank receipt to the accounting ledger and retain payment proof, especially where funds originate outside the EEA.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro supplier payments and SWIFT customer-credit transfers, commonly represented operationally by an MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA payments. Include accurate ordering-customer, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, contract, and purpose information. For higher-value or documentary transactions, use a commercial letter of credit issued or confirmed by a regulated bank, with documentary collection or open-account settlement only after counterparty and trade-risk assessment. Match payments to purchase orders, invoices, customs and transport records, and goods-receipt evidence. Apply segregation of duties, dual approval, sanctions screening, beneficiary-account verification, and payment-message consistency controls. Card and Stripe receipts should settle into a controlled collection account and be reconciled to processor reports, refunds, reserves, fees, VAT, and chargebacks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts with an EU-regulated bank for forecast or committed foreign-currency receipts and payments, subject to documented hedging purpose, counterparty onboarding, confirmation, valuation, and accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency, bank, jurisdiction, and transaction are legally and commercially eligible; settlement is normally in euros or another agreed currency against a reference rate, and the instrument remains subject to bank suitability, derivatives documentation, EMIR, reporting, collateral, and risk-management requirements.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for longer-term funding or recurring currency exposure, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, counterparty credit approval, collateral terms, valuation, and EMIR obligations where applicable.

Foreign-exchange options or option structures where approved by the bank and demonstrably connected to an underlying commercial exposure; review premium, leverage, early-termination, margin, and accounting consequences before execution.

Natural hedging through matching currency receipts and payments, currency-denominated supplier contracts, and centralized netting, provided the arrangements are commercially documented, properly priced, and reconciled.

Do not use speculative, leveraged, or third-party FX arrangements outside the company's approved treasury policy; ensure derivatives are executed through appropriately authorised counterparties and recorded under applicable French and EU accounting and regulatory requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social security declaration (Déclaration Sociale Nominative - DSN) year-end summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing by January 31 for the preceding calendar year end, aligned with payroll reporting cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 1.5% of gross payroll per month or part thereof, capped at 3.8%; potential criminal sanctions for willful non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax return for commercial companies (Déclaration de Résultat - n° 2065)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second business day following May 1 for calendar-year taxpayers, or within three months after fiscal year-end close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of EUR 50 plus 0.5% of assessed tax per month; interest at monthly rate of 0.14%; formal assessment may trigger 10% late filing penalty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and tax annexes (Liasse Fiscale n° 2050 series)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as corporate income tax return, normally by May 2 following the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic 5% increase in corporate income tax if return is late, plus default interest; severe non-filing may trigger EUR 1,500 penalty and loss of audit deductions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' approval of annual accounts and allocation of results (Assemblée Générale Ordinaire Annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting recorded in minutes; filing of audited accounts at the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGOA must be held within six months of fiscal year-end unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability of managers for breach of duty; possible court-ordered convocation; non-filing of approved accounts within 30 days renders company subject to strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual filing of approved financial statements at the Commercial and Companies Registry (Dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Infogreffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after AGOA approval, or two months if paper filing, and no later than nine months after fiscal year-end in practice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EUR 1,200 for failure to file accounts; court summons for directors; registry may issue injunction and initiate administrative strike-off after one year of non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Confirmation of beneficial ownership declaration (Déclaration de Bénéficiaires Effectifs - DBE) update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Mandatory update within 30 days of any change in shareholding or beneficial owner; annual verification with annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Adminstrative fine up to EUR 750 for natural persons and EUR 3,750 for legal entities; possible six-month imprisonment fine if omission is intentional

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of company data and payment of registration fee (Régularisation annuelle au Registre National des Entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before December 31 of each calendar year, associated with annual return filing and change notifications
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry fees accrue; company published as non-compliant; repeated failure triggers judicial dissolution procedure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statement of equal pay index (Index Égalité Professionnelle Femmes-Hommes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Labour (Ministère du Travail); publication on company website and communication to CSE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each year by March 1 for the previous calendar year, mandatory for companies with at least 50 employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Salary increase penalty up to 1% of total payroll; unavailable if no index published; potential EUR 2,000 fine for non-publication

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual real estate levy declaration for business premises (Déclaration de Taxe Foncière and Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises - CFE if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE declaration by December 31 prior to the tax year and payment by December 15; actual levy based on prior-year returned data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 5% plus monthly interest of 0.4%; seizure of company assets for prolonged non-payment; no strike-off solely for local tax issue

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit required where any two of the following exceed thresholds for two consecutive years: total balance sheet EUR 6,000,000; net turnover EUR 12,000,000; average workforce of 100 employees; specific audit also required for majority-owned subsidiaries of higher-tier companies or where shareholders holding 10% of capital petition court.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Règlement ANC n° 2014-03) as transposed under the French Commercial Code; consolidated entities must apply IFRS as adopted by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each SARL must maintain and confirm an accurate register of beneficial owners every year along with the annual return. Any transfer of shares or change in control exceeding 25% of capital or voting rights requires a DBE declaration to the RNE within 30 days, and the annual confirmation must state that no unreported changes have occurred.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 4,000 to EUR 15,000 for non-listed small SARL under full periodic audit; EUR 2,000 to EUR 5,000 for simplified review

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on taxable profits up to EUR 42,500 for qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises meeting the statutory thresholds; research tax credit (Créance d'Impôt Recherche) calculated at up to 30% of eligible research and development expenditures, subject to caps and carryforward rules; Young Innovative Company (Jeune Entreprise Innovante) exemption available for up to 8 fiscal years on qualifying R&D-dominated businesses

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (liassex fiscale) and related annexes filed via the professional online portal at impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel / EFI) or through EDI (Échange de Données Informatisé); Form 2571 for annual tax return summary
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is the second business day after 1 May following the close of the fiscal year; for fiscal years ending 31 December, the deadline is generally 3 May of the subsequent calendar year (or the next business day if 3 May falls on a weekend/holiday)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate taxable income or deficit after deducting all deductible expenses and applying any tax loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL must report income attributable to its French permanent establishment; utilise Box 1 to declare the French-source taxable result, translating EUR-denominated accounts, and attach the certificate of effective management location where required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net short-term and long-term capital gains or losses subject to preferential corporate tax treatment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gains from disposal of French business assets; foreign tax credit claims require supporting DTA position; attach Form 2059-CG and any applicable treaty annex

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax loss carryforward available at the beginning of the fiscal year, amounts used in the current year, and remaining balance carried forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities can only utilise losses generated by the French permanent establishment against French-source income; complete the movement table and ensure no foreign head-office losses are mixed in

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Various tax credits, including research tax credit, competitiveness and employment tax credit (CICE discontinued), and international tax credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Research tax credit relief is only available for R&D activities carried on in France; Annex 2069-A and related declarations must be prepared; treaty tax credits must be cross-referenced to the relevant DTA article

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax deductions granted for specific investments, donations, or incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Generally not available for non-resident entities except for narrowly defined French investment incentives; state any treaty-protected entitlement on the return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional 3.3% social contribution on the portion of corporate income tax exceeding EUR 763,000 for companies with turnover above EUR 250 million
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL with French PE must evaluate the turnover threshold on a worldwide consolidated basis; exemption applies below statutory thresholds

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 (Résultat net fiscal et tableaux annexes)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting net income to taxable result, including non-deductible charges and tax-exempt revenues
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepare Tableau 2058-A and 2058-B on uniform French chart of accounts; align transfer pricing adjustments with TP documentation and maintain contemporaneous evidence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual turnover and average employee headcount for SME-reduced-rate eligibility and digital tax thresholds
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include French PE turnover only; comparability with intra-group transactions must be consistent with transfer pricing disclosures

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on the tax due (40% if the return is filed within 30 days of a formal notice and 80% if filed more than 30 days after the formal notice); interest for late payment accrues at 0.20% per month; intentional omission can lead to additional penalties of up to 40% of the unpaid tax and criminal prosecution for tax evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (French withholding tax on dividends distributed by a French company to non-resident shareholders, subject to Directive 2011/96/EU parent-subsidiary exemption where applicable, and subject to 12.8% flat tax for EU/EEA individuals under specific conditions, but corporate non-resident shareholders are generally exposed to 25% absent relief)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the beneficial owner must submit a validation request (demande de rescrit) for reduced withholding via Form 5000 / 5001 or provide a French tax residence certificate (Formulaire 5030) and the relevant DTA article analysis before the payment date; the French Financial Act imposes a condition of actual tax residence in the treaty jurisdiction and requires the recipient to be the beneficial owner; for EU parent companies the parent-subsidiary directive exemption is claimed by submitting Form 5052 or by filing for a refund where withholding has been levied; refund claims must be lodged within the statutory deadline (generally the second year following the year of taxation) and must be accompanied by certificate of residence from the foreign tax authority
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalties: 33.33% (or 30%) for patent and similar rights under French domestic law; treaty rates generally reduced to 0% (licences of copyrights for software/patents in most OECD DTAs require effective taxation in the residence state), 10% or 15% depending on the treaty; statutory interest withholding: 30% on deemed French-source interest paid to non-residents unless the recipient is an EU/EEA company holding a qualifying interest and directive relief applies; French anti-abuse provisions require substance and beneficial ownership analysis before treaty relief

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000 (no statutory transfer pricing documentation obligation for the automatic Local File/Master File where annual related-party transactions remain below EUR 400,000, but the French tax administration can request documentation on taxpayer initiative and penalties apply for incomplete documentation)
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies substantial economic substance and anti-abuse doctrines, including the abuse of law procedure (procédure de l'abus de droit), the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR), the principal purpose test under DAC6, and the French subsidiary economic substance requirement for treaty benefits; for the AI robotic pet sector, a French SARL must demonstrate operational substance through local R&D, employment of qualified engineers, actual product design or assembly oversight, physical premises, and active management decisions; failure to demonstrate substance for tax resident status or treaty relief triggers re-characterisation of arrangements and denial of tax treaty benefits

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of taxable sales, underreporting of French-source revenue from interactive AI pet robot sales, failure to declare a permanent establishment, or artificial transfer of profits to low-tax jurisdictions via inflated royalty payments or service fees without economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of EUR 500,000 (or up to double the amount evaded) and imprisonment of up to 7 years; confiscation of assets; administrative penalties of up to 80% of the understated tax plus daily surcharges and publication of the sanction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable to pay the corporate tax arrears through the abuse of law doctrine and directors' tort liability (faute de gestion); criminal conviction leads to imprisonment and travel bans; French courts can disallow the separate personality of the SARL (actio pauliana) where assets were fraudulently diverted

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or produce contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation under Article L.13 AA of the French Tax Procedure Book, or incompatible intra-group pricing for AI robot hardware, embedded software royalties, or marketing and distribution services benefiting a foreign related entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mandatory documentation penalties of up to 5% of the gross amount of the undocumented transfers or EUR 10,000, plus adjustive tax reassessments, late interest and 40% penalties for lack of good faith or 80% for serious misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved distorted transfer prices may face personal liability for restitution of tax damage caused to the SARL, disqualification from management functions, civil damages under corporate law, and criminal sanctions in cases of deliberate misstatement

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangements and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Abusing a French SARL as a conduit or artificial booking centre in a cross-border AI pet robot supply chain with no real employees, no functions and risks managed in France, and passive receipt of global margins, or invoking a French tax treaty for a resident of a third state (treaty shopping)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterisation of the entity under DAC6 and ATAD rules, reclassification of profits as constructive dividends subject to withholding tax, penalty of up to 100% of the re-characterised tax advantage, and nullification of legal acts under abuse of law procedure with interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for abuse of law where directors knowingly executed sham arrangements; foreign directors face immobility measures, seizure of assets located in France, and potential extradition for criminal tax fraud if accomplice liability is established

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling large volumes of third-country retail payments for robotic toys without performing KYC/CDD, failure to declare cash transactions above EUR 10,000 for business trade, or using convoluted payment chains to obscure beneficial ownership of the SARL's shareholders or the source of funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the French Monetary and Financial Code, fines up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for laundering; Tracfin referrals and asset forfeiture; suspension of banking licences or prohibition from accepting payments via Stripe/credit cards
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate directors and compliance officers are personally subject to criminal liability for failure to establish AML compliance, mandatory reporting of suspicious transactions, and beneficial ownership transparency (RBE); non-resident directors may be prohibited from opening a bank account in France and removed from corporate registry

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend or Interest Withholding Tax Evasion and Profit Repatriation without DTA Protocol
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to a foreign shareholder/enjoying profits without accounting for the statutory 25% withholding tax, claiming treaty relief without valid tax residence certificate or substance, or disguising distributions as tax-exempt royalty payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax assessments, 40% to 80% penalties for bad faith or intentional concealment, late payment interest of 0.20% per month, plus joint and several liability of the paying company for the unreported withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers who knowingly fail to withhold and remit dividends tax are personally liable for the tax under article 1754 of the French General Tax Code; criminal conviction can extend to directors' personal bank accounts and real estate through asset seizure and restrictive travel bans
